Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time today. Attached: RDW-MAP-Medivue-v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones) and a short markdown that lists the acceptance tests.

High level summary:
- Evaluation window: 3 weeks (pilot integration + smoke + live-run checkpoint)
- Goal: Validate integration, latency & throughput at representative load, and model output fidelity on Medivue de-identified sample prompts
- Primary exit gates: smoke pass, integration end-to-end, acceptance test pass (see attached), legal/compliance evidence delivered

Key asks for Medivue:
1) Confirm target business outcomes we should measure (e.g., triage reduction, annotation time saved)
2) Share a representative de-identified prompt corpus for quality tests (CSV or S3 link)
3) Confirm who owns running acceptance tests vs. Redwood-run verification (we can do both)

Proposed next steps: review the MAP, call next Wed to finalize timeline, and lock the acceptance test owner.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once I get confirmation on times.

Adding a CS perspective and suggested concrete acceptance thresholds we typically use for pilots like this. Notes below — I’ve also annotated the attached acceptance-tests doc in place (see medivue-eval-acceptance-tests.md).

Suggested acceptance criteria (pilot):
- Functional smoke: all endpoints respond and auth flows succeed (within 24 hours of integration)
- Latency: median token-generation latency < 120ms; p95 end-to-end response for the most common prompt set < 250ms (server-side inference only)
- Throughput: able to sustain steady 50 rps for 10 minutes with <5% error rate in our staging config (adjustable per your expected traffic profile)
- Quality: automated pass rate on your annotated sample >= 82% (per the quality rubric in the doc)
- Security/compliance evidence: proof of SOC 2 scoping, data residency confirmation, and audit log access for the test window

Who runs tests?
- Redwood-run verification: we can execute a blind verification run and share raw logs and tooling outputs.
- Medivue-run acceptance: your team runs one end-to-end acceptance run with our monitoring hooks enabled; results are used for sign-off.

If these look reasonable I’ll update the MAP with explicit owners per milestone and a small test-run playbook.

—
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Thanks Grace, Lena — I’ve incorporated the thresholds and fleshed out the exit gates in the attached acceptance-tests doc (medivue-eval-acceptance-tests.md). Key updates:

Exit gates (detailed):
1) Smoke gate — successful auth + sample inference for 20 canonical prompts (pass >= 95% success)
2) Integration gate — E2E flows with your staging environment + basic telemetry (p95 < 250ms)
3) Quality gate — annotated test set concordance >= 82% and no high-severity hallucination mode in top-50 samples
4) Compliance gate — signed evidence for SOC 2 scoping items we enumerated + confirmation of log access for the test window

Fallbacks & operational notes:
- If latency exceeds p95 threshold during integration, Redwood recommends enabling KV prefix caching + a light quantized variant to meet targets. We’ll send a config suggestion in the MAP.
- For data controls: we can run the verification in our Dedicated environment (isolated tenant) if Medivue requires it — that would be a short procurement addendum.

I’ve attached the updated test matrix and a short runbook. Can we lock the sign-off meeting for Aug 10 to review results and finalize the PO? I’ll create the invite for 10:00 PT on Aug 10 unless you prefer another time.

—
Sergio Alvarez
